context.long: Shortest window — captures anaerobic peaks (hill sprint, attack). Barely trainable, largely genetic.
VO2max range. Can be targeted with high-intensity intervals (4×5 min).
Long interval or short tempo effort. Borderline between anaerobic and aerobic.
The most important value: roughly matches your lactate threshold HR. Typically around 85–92% of HRmax.
Aerobic range. How well can you hold a high HR over an hour? Shows your aerobic base.

explainer.body: For every time window (1 min to 60 min), the algorithm searches all your rides for the highest average heart rate over exactly that many consecutive seconds. The result shows how high your HR peaked at different effort durations — similar to a power curve, but without a power meter.
explainer.title: What does this curve show?

curve.footerNote: Calculation: rolling maximum of second-by-second HR across all FIT tracks. Only activities with HR data are included. Short windows can be skewed by brief sprints — the 20-minute value is the most meaningful.

interpretation.steepnessFlat: Very flat — strong aerobic base, you can sustain a high HR even over long durations.
interpretation.steepnessModerate: Moderate — good balance between endurance and intensity.
interpretation.steepnessSteep: Steep — a big peak over short durations, but HR drops off sharply over longer ones. More base training helps.
interpretation.thresholdBody: Corresponds to your 20-minute best. The lactate threshold is typically around 85–92% of HRmax and marks the transition from aerobic to anaerobic metabolism.
